p.t: In short
p.s: Video, ad creative and content production tools

p.t:
Before you edit, make one folder for each ad's pictures and videos.
Never rename or move a file after you import it into an editor. The link to it breaks.

Start with CapCut. It is free, quick, and the desktop (computer) version is best for ad work.
Good light matters more than a good camera.
Use Splice to edit TikTok ads and product videos. Use InShot for videos that go to several platforms.
Check Splice's price in the app store first. Two different prices are stated.
Before making long AI voice audio with ElevenLabs, check your plan's character limit (how much text it can convert).
Before uploading AI-made images to Meta, re-download them through Canva. This removes hidden data that Meta can read to spot AI content.
To make a wide video tall for social ad spots, use a separate online editor.
Video, ad creative and content production tools
Planning the project folder and assets
1. Create a **Google Drive** folder (online file storage) for the campaign.
p.h: Organise assets before building any ad

p.t: 2. Inside it, create **two** subfolders: "Image Assets" and "Video Assets".
3. Gather all images: AliExpress product photos, Instagram posts, user-generated content (UGC, pictures or videos made by ordinary customers or creators), screenshots.
4. Gather all videos: TikTok product clips, Instagram Reels (short vertical videos on Instagram), YouTube Shorts (short videos on YouTube), self-filmed footage.
5. Add **product images**, lifestyle images (photos of the product in real life) and platform-specific clips (clips sized and styled for one app, such as TikTok).
6. Reference this folder when designing ad creatives (ad images and videos) in **Canva** (an online design tool) to keep them consistent and fast.
Set up the folders in this order **before importing anything** (importing means bringing files into the editor):

1. **Create** a separate assets folder for images, emojis and graphics.
2. **Create** a separate audio folder for voiceovers, music and sound effects.
3. **Create** a separate video folder for stock footage (ready-made clips you can use) and product clips.
4. **Keep** these folders stable. Moving or renaming files breaks the links in editing software such as Premiere Pro (a professional video editor), which then reports that the files cannot be found.
**Renaming or moving** a source file (the original file you start from) or its folder after import breaks the link to the clip, so keep raw footage (unedited original video) in fixed locations.
Folders inside a Premiere Pro project bin (a folder inside the project window) only organise your work and do not affect links to source files. Use import folders such as assets, audio and video.
**Google Drive, Dropbox or an external hard drive** (a separate disk you plug in) can store project folders.
Cloud storage (files kept on the internet) lets you reach the same files from a phone, for example to download clips or upload recorded voiceovers.
When importing downloaded clips into CapCut, choose **"Stay in original location"** in the Imported media pop-up to keep the files in their download folder instead of copying them.
Recording and UGC Gear
Low-cost lighting
p.s: Video, ad creative and content production tools

p.t: A pair of second-hand LED lights (energy-saving lights), for example from Facebook Marketplace, costs about **20 USD** in total.
A basic ring light (a round light that fits around the camera) costs about 10 to 15 USD on average.
A simple coil light (a light shaped like a loop) with an umbrella diffuser (a soft cover that spreads light) works well as a key light (the main light on the subject) and softens harsh light.
**Lighting** affects product video quality more than camera hardware.
A phone selfie stick costing about **20 USD** extends and folds into a small tripod (a three-legged stand) that stands on a desk,
giving steady footage of a phone recording.
A clip-on microphone for the iPhone's Lightning port (the iPhone's charging plug) has a companion app (a matching phone app) for adjusting its settings.

It records good audio only when it stays fairly close to the phone.
**Voice Memos** (the free iPhone recording app) records audio that can be shared to Splice (a video editing app).
**Keynote or PowerPoint** (slide programs) can build a slideshow video from product images and slides, with recorded narration (spoken explanation) over the slides, before uploading to YouTube.
Sourcing footage: downloads, stock and creator discovery
**4K Video Downloader** (a computer app) saves YouTube videos to your computer. Copy the YouTube link, paste it into the app and download the file.
The app asked for payment on at least one download, so check its terms (rules) before relying on it.
The same app can download a sound effect as an MP3 (a common audio file). See the sound effect steps under CapCut.
**SnapTik** downloads TikTok videos: paste the TikTok link and save the file. SnapInsta is an alternative for similar downloads.
Snaptik, ssstik and Downloader Bot download TikTok videos. Snaptik is the one used for this step in this example.
A downloader such as SnapTik can save a finished TikTok so it can be **reposted** to Instagram Reels.
A **video-to-text extractor** (a tool that turns spoken words in a video into written text) converts the spoken script of a direct-response ad (an ad that asks people to buy now) into text.
Paste the text into an AI chat as a model (an example to copy) and ask for a new ad for your own audience. This saves typing the copy (the sales words) by hand.
Stock footage and images
p.s: Video, ad creative and content production tools

p.t: **Pexels and Unsplash** are free stock footage (ready-made clips) sites.
Use them to find pain-point clips (clips that show the problem your product solves) when you have no product footage yet, then add grayscale treatment (black and white)
and caption overlays (text placed on top of the picture).
**Envato Elements** is a third-party subscription library (a paid membership from another company) of graphics, stock video, imagery, sound effects and video effects for use in Photoshop
and Illustrator (design programs). Photoshop and Illustrator do not include such a library, so a separate asset source is needed.
**Envato Elements** is a royalty-free stock library (pay once, then use without paying each time). Build ad visuals by cutting out stock images, adding backgrounds and placing text on top.
This is slower than generating images with ChatGPT from reference ads.
**Envato Elements** is a monthly subscription for stock photos and other design assets with unlimited downloads. It is an alternative to buying single images or using supplier images.
**Envato Elements** was a subscription source for images, design assets and templates used by the team.
The Envato stock video subscription costs about **200 USD per year** and includes graphics, sound effects and stock footage.
**Modash** finds creators (people who post content) by niche (topic) and engagement rate (how many people like, comment and share).
Use it to shortlist creators for UGC content before contacting them.

Principles for choosing
p.s: Video, ad creative and content production tools

p.t: CapCut is quick to start on a phone or desktop. Desktop editors such as Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve suit serious production.
If you plan to produce ads regularly, pick **one** desktop editor and learn it properly.
Premiere Pro, Final Cut and DaVinci Resolve are heavier (slower and bigger) but offer more functionality.
CapCut is cheaper and easier for beginners and already includes graphics, sound effects and auto captions (text the app writes from speech).
Splice is practical for beginners making short-form ads, but it cannot place sound effects or cuts at split-second precision (exact timing to a tiny fraction of a second).

For **frame-level timing** (timing down to one single picture in a video), use DaVinci Resolve or Final Cut Pro on Mac. Use Splice for most edits and switch to the desktop editor only when precise timing matters.
**Test** an editor before committing. Principles transfer between tools, so switching later is low-risk.
Premiere Pro often requires buying a transition package (a set of extra effects you pay for) before transitions can be used.
CapCut ships a large set of transitions (effects that join two clips) such as zoom, wipe and shake that can be added directly.
For beginners who need quick transitions without extra purchases, CapCut is the faster starting point.
InVideo and Contagion are video editing tools. One of them was used to edit short ads in this example.
CapCut is a free video editor from the company behind TikTok.
For ad creative work, **CapCut desktop** (the computer version) is preferred over the mobile app because all recorded footage can be imported at once, edited
and saved in a project file (one saved file that holds the whole edit). The free basic plan is sufficient for beginners.
CapCut on a phone is fast and capable, but it stores everything on the phone and is less efficient for managing video projects than desktop software. Large projects are inefficient on a phone.
**CapCut Pro** costs 10 US dollars per month and adds more transitions, extra effects and a larger library of graphics and sound effects. Beginners do not need it to produce Facebook ad creatives.

The free library covers basic transitions, effects and text animations. Text templates, some animations and additional pro transitions require Pro. For a beginner ad workflow, the free items are enough to start.
Paid items are worth adding only once the basic edit is working.
Some animation options, such as advanced animated captions, may require a Pro account (a paid plan). Check whether a feature is locked before building an ad template around it.
Layout (desktop)
p.s: Video, ad creative and content production tools

p.t: Layout means how the screen is arranged.
The **media bin (the panel that holds your files) holds imported footage, sounds and images. The timeline (the bar at the bottom where clips are placed in order) layers clips.**

**The player** (the preview screen) in the middle shows the output. The right-side control panel changes the selected asset. The control panel holds volume, speed, animation and other settings for the selection.
The timeline is at the bottom and holds all video, audio and graphics tracks (rows that stack layers). The preview window is in the middle.
The left panel has the tabs Media, Audio, Text, Stickers, Effects, Filters, Adjustment and Templates.
The right panel is the Tools area, which changes with the selected clip and controls position, scale (size) and other properties.
**Click** any imported file in the Media panel to play it in the preview window. Review footage there before dragging it onto the timeline.

**Scrub** footage (drag across the preview to move through it) before placing it on the timeline, to check what each clip contains. Dragging a clip onto the timeline makes it the active track for layering.
The video preview sits at the top, the timeline in the middle and the main menu at the bottom with Edit, Audio, Text and Stickers.
Under Edit, the **Split** option cuts the clip at the playhead (the marker that shows the current spot).
**Frame rate is how many pictures a video shows each second, written as fps.**
**Shoot and edit at 30 fps**, but check the frame rate your camera or phone actually recorded and match the project to it.
Under the CapCut menu, Edit settings offers a **proxy** option (a small, lighter copy of your footage) that caches media (stores a temporary copy) so a weaker computer runs more smoothly.
Recorded footage at **1920 x 1080 pixels** is the landscape format (wide screen; pixels are the tiny dots that make up a picture), useful when searching for horizontal footage.
Shortcuts and timeline controls
p.s: Video, ad creative and content production tools

p.t: **A**: selection tool (the arrow that picks and moves clips). **B**: blade (cut) tool.

**Ctrl+B**: splits the clip under the cursor without switching tools.
**Space**: plays from the playhead, and pressing it again stops playback.

**Left and right arrow keys** step through frames. Shift plus arrow keys moves faster.
**A selects and moves clips. B** activates the blade to cut.
**Ctrl/Cmd+Z** undoes. Ctrl/Cmd plus mouse wheel zooms the timeline.
**Zoom the timeline** by holding Ctrl or Cmd and scrolling. This helps when checking small cuts or the audio waveform (the picture of sound as a wave), and shows where speech starts and stops.
Keep **Snap** switched on as a beginner. Snap makes clips lock to the ends of neighbouring clips and avoids small gaps.
Snap is the toggle near the timeline controls and can be turned off when free placement is needed.
Clips **snap** to the edges of neighbouring clips when you drag them. This helps line up B-roll (extra footage laid over the main clip) and transition points without manual measuring.
On mobile, **hold** a timeline item with your thumb and drag. The item vibrates when it nears an edge, which helps it snap into position.
The **audio waveform** under each clip makes pauses and silent gaps visible.

Use it to find cut points for filler words (um, uh, like) before you play the A-roll (the main talking footage) back.
Remove filler or a mistake:

1. **Play** the footage and find the mistake or filler.
2. Switch to the blade tool with **B** and cut at the start and end of the unwanted section.
3. Switch back to the selection tool with **A** and click the unwanted piece.

4. Press **Delete or Backspace** to remove it. The gap closes automatically, so the remaining clips move together.
5. **Replay** the section and repeat until the take is clean.
In selection mode, **grab** the edge of a clip and drag it inward or outward to shorten or lengthen it. This trims (cuts off the ends) without the blade.

Deleting a clip with Backspace closes the gap it leaves, so the next clip shifts left.
**Drag a selection box** across several clips on the timeline to move or delete them together.
To select several layers, drag a selection box over them or hold **Cmd (Mac) or Ctrl** (Windows) while clicking each one. You can then move them or change their text style together.
Speed
p.s: Video, ad creative and content production tools

p.t: To change a clip's playback speed, select the clip and use the **Speed** control in the video section of the right-hand control panel.
A 2x playback shortcut (double speed for the whole timeline) like the one in Premiere Pro was not shown here, so speed changes are made on the clip itself.
On mobile, open **Speed** on a clip. Normal changes the whole clip evenly.
Curve changes speed over time to create a speed ramp (a speed that changes gradually), for example slow at the start and fast at the end.
A **keyframe** (a marker that saves a setting at one moment) stores a value such as position or scale at one point in time.
The clip animates between two or more keyframes, which creates movement such as following a subject or zooming in on a product.
Keyframes can animate more than scale, including opacity (how see-through something is), position, rotation, size and alignment, using one keyframe at the start and one at the end.

For example, a fade-in text is made by keyframing opacity from zero to full.
Add a moving zoom or pan (a slow zoom or sideways move) in CapCut:

1. **Add** a keyframe with the diamond button beside the play button.
2. **Move** the playhead.
3. **Change** the scale to zoom.
4. **Repeat** for each position change to make a moving zoom or pan.
The keyframe button sits beside the play button. Tapping it places a red diamond at the current position. To remove a keyframe, hover over the diamond until it turns red and tap the minus option.
**Motion blur** in the adjustment settings adds blur to movement so it looks more like real camera motion. Use a light setting, because heavy blur looks unnatural.
**Fade out:** grab the end of the clip, drag to adjust its length, then choose Fade from the bottom menu and select fade out so the clip ends by fading to black.
Split a clip at the playhead, click the small white marker between the two clips and choose a transition from the Movement category, such as Pull out,
Pull in, Shake or Zoom. Adjust the **transition length** after it is applied.
On mobile, **tap** the point between two clips to open the transition presets (ready-made settings), which include zooms, flashes and burns. Choose one to join the clips.
Audio, sound effects and text-to-speech
p.s: Video, ad creative and content production tools

p.t: Add a sound effect to a CapCut ad:

1. **Search** YouTube for a sound effect, for example by typing sfx and the effect name.
2. **Copy** the video link and download it as an MP3 with 4K Video Downloader.

3. **Import** the MP3 into CapCut.
4. **Place** the sound on the timeline at the moment it should play.
**Built-in text-to-speech** (the app reads text aloud in a computer voice): tap the text-to-speech button in the bottom menu, type the script and choose a voice preset.
CapCut belongs to the company behind TikTok, so it often adds features suited to TikTok content.

Add a voiceover from **ElevenLabs** (an online AI voice tool) in CapCut:
1. **Type** the script into ElevenLabs and generate the voiceover.

2. **Download** the generated audio file.
3. In CapCut, use the audio import option to **upload** the file.
4. **Merge** the imported audio with your video track in the timeline.
Recommended order in CapCut:
1. **Record** or film the main talking-head footage (A-roll, the person speaking to the camera), either as UGC or as a typical ad, from a finished script.
2. **Cut out** filler words, pauses and mistakes from the A-roll and play it through to check the script.

3. **Overlay** B-roll product shots (extra shots of the product) on top of the A-roll while the speaker talks.
4. **Add** background music and sound effects.

5. **Add** auto captions and style them.
6. **Add** graphics such as icons, checkmarks and bullet points.
7. **Add** transitions, cuts, zooms and keyframed motion.
CapCut is used to make video creatives by combining clips, text, descriptions and AI voiceovers. It is a common editor for building several ad variations quickly.

CapCut cuts downloaded ad videos down to their **hook** (the first few seconds that catch attention), combines clips from different ads into one new creative and exports (saves the finished file) the result.
The workflow runs entirely on the downloaded files.
Premiere pro and daVinci resolve (continued)
p.s: Video, ad creative and content production tools

p.t: Premiere pro and daVinci resolve
**Premiere Pro is a professional video editor used alongside After Effects** (a motion graphics program) for motion graphics (moving titles and shapes).
Panels (boxes of tools on screen): the **Project panel (bottom left) holds imported media and bins.**
**The Timeline (bottom) shows clips in sequence, with visual tracks above and audio tracks below a divider. The Program monitor (center) previews the combined result.**
**The Effect Controls** panel (top) edits the selected clip.

A new **sequence** (a timeline with its own size settings) takes the aspect ratio (the shape, such as wide or tall) of the first clip you add. Create a separate sequence for vertical video so the ratio is correct.

Check the ratio before editing, because the sequence settings follow the first imported clip.
Set up a project:
1. **Create** a dated project folder for the product.

2. **Create** bins for video, audio and assets inside the project.
3. **Import** the downloaded clip and drag it onto the timeline.

4. **Keep** visual tracks above the divider and audio tracks below it.
5. **Place** extra footage such as B-roll on higher visual tracks.
The **selection tool grabs and moves clips on the timeline. The razor tool cuts a clip where you click. Its shortcut is C in Premiere Pro and X** in DaVinci Resolve.
Effect Controls for a clip include position (left and right, up and down), scale, rotation, opacity or visibility, and clip speed. Adjust these per clip in the Effect Controls panel.

**Scrubbing** means dragging the playhead along the timeline to move back and forth through footage. This is how you review and find cut points.
Duplicate a text layer:

1. **Select** the text layer.
2. **Hold** Alt on Windows or Option on Mac.
3. **Drag** the layer out to create a copy.
4. **Repeat** to build a set of text layers, then edit each one's wording and position.
**Essential Sound panel** (Premiere's audio helper): use it to set each audio clip's type, such as Dialogue, Background music or Sound effects,
Premiere Pro (continued)
p.s: Video, ad creative and content production tools

p.t: and apply the matching preset (ready-made setting) for balanced voice levels.
**Set** a voiceover clip to Dialogue and choose the preset "balanced male voice" to clean up and balance the recording. Adjust the volume afterwards if needed.

**Lower** the clip volume first if the audio is too loud.
Keep settings basic. Adjust clip volume, and turn **reverb** (a room echo effect) or echo off if they are not needed.
**Tick-tok style text overlay: add a text layer with Open Sans Bold (a font, which is a style of letters) and adjust the line height** (the space between lines of text) in the text settings.
Place the text with the Vector Motion position controls (Premiere's position settings) so it sits clear of the product.
A fast zoom transition can be added from the Effects panel using a **zoom blur preset**, placed between two clips.

Third-party presets (add-ons from other makers) such as Film Impact or Premiere Composer provide more zoom transitions.
Create a zoom-in keyframe:

1. **Select** the clip and open Effect Controls > Transform.
2. **Move** the anchor point onto the product or subject you want to zoom towards.

3. **Set** a keyframe on Scale at the start of the move.
4. **Move** the playhead forward and change the Scale value to zoom in, which creates a second keyframe.
5. **Check** the motion in playback and adjust the anchor point if the subject drifts off centre.
**Right-click a keyframe and choose Ease In or Ease Out** to create smooth speed curves (ease means a slow start or slow end). Use the speed graph for custom curves when a preset is not enough.
**DaVinci Resolve** by Blackmagic Design is free and includes most of the functions of Premiere Pro, making it a budget option for video editing.
It covers most functions of Premiere Pro for basic editing work and is a budget-friendly option for beginners.
It is a free desktop editor with a layout similar to Premiere Pro. It has a folder section for organising media and drags clips onto a timeline, but its shortcuts differ.
The preset "balanced background music" applies a finished music mix once you place a music track.
Splice, inShot, edits, iMovie and tikTok's editor (continued)
p.s: Video, ad creative and content production tools

p.t: Splice, inShot, edits, iMovie and tikTok's editor
Splice is a phone editing app (it also works on a computer).
It is used for cutting, voiceovers (recorded narration), speed changes, slow motion and pulling out sounds. **Splice is preferred over TikTok's editor for product videos.**
Cost: about **$12 per month**. One statement says $12 per year, so verify the price in the app store.
Splice is used to edit TikTok ads.
It matches on-screen text (words shown on the video) to speech, and it adds non-copyrighted sounds (sounds you can use without a copyright owner's permission) **before upload**.
Splice is a mobile (phone) and desktop (computer) editing app. The advice was **to edit on a phone** and send the file to a computer.
Splice works better on iPhone because TikTok allows higher-quality uploads from iOS (Apple's phone system). Uploads from Android (Google's phone system) are limited.
Android phones are still viable.
InShot is a mobile (phone) video editor. It is used to edit creator content (videos made by content creators) before uploading it to social platforms.
InShot is not tied to any single platform, so its exports (the finished saved files) are easier to reuse elsewhere. **Use InShot** for content that goes to several platforms.
Platform-native text tools (text tools built into each app) in Instagram, TikTok and YouTube Shorts add overlay text (words placed on top of the video) in each platform's own fonts and style.
This happens **when the video is uploaded**.
Edits (Instagram)
p.s: Video, ad creative and content production tools

p.t: Edits is a separate mobile video editing app made by Instagram. It is Instagram's counterpart to CapCut (a popular video editor).
**It is a standalone download**, not a feature inside the regular Instagram app.
Edits offers more editing options than Instagram's built-in reel editor (the editor inside Instagram for short vertical videos called reels). These include more fonts and animations.
Edits removes many of the built-in editor's limitations. **The built-in reel editor is still more restricted.**
The Edits app has five main tabs (sections you switch between): Ideas, Reels, Edits, Record and Inspiration.
**Inspiration is opened with the plus icon** at the bottom of the screen.
The Reels tab shows videos similar to your own, or videos the app recommends you produce.

The Edits tab is the project gallery (your list of work). It holds current projects and drafts (unfinished versions).
Projects can be sorted by **date created** or alphabetically.
Recording inside the Edits app allows up to **10 minutes** per clip.

How Edits' export metadata (hidden information saved in a file, such as how it was made) behaves after re-uploading to other platforms is **unknown**. Use InShot for content that goes to several platforms.
iMovie covers basic cuts and transitions (the effects between two clips) for simple video edits.

iMovie is enough for basic cuts, cropping and simple transitions on UGC (user-generated content, videos made by ordinary people or customers) or repurposed footage (old footage reused in a new video).
**Use a separate online editor** when a clip must be converted to vertical format (tall, phone-screen shape) for social placements (the spots in social apps where an ad appears).
Online editors are used to convert formats, for example **making a video vertical** for ads.
TikTok's built-in editor is **fast** for quick trims (cutting off the start or end) and small fixes. It does not re-render (rebuild) a full project.

If TikTok's text-to-speech timing (when the computer voice speaks) jumps around and will not stay in place:
Restarting the phone did not fix it.

**Uninstalling and reinstalling the app** did fix it.
Try reinstalling before you change the content.
Voiceover and Text-to-Speech (continued)
p.s: Video, ad creative and content production tools

p.t: Voiceover and Text-to-Speech
ElevenLabs is an AI voice tool.
It converts a script (the written text) into speech in a chosen voice and supports multilingual output (more than one language).
Non-English languages need **the multilingual option**.
Several text-to-speech tools (tools that read written text aloud) were compared. ElevenLabs sounded the most natural to the creator.
ElevenLabs generates AI voiceovers that can be added to short video creatives (short ads). **Use it when you need narration** without recording your own voice.

ElevenLabs is used to make **the voice in ads AI-generated**.
Setup:
1. Choose a voice.

2. Optionally change the voice settings.
3. Check the languages offered under the multilingual option.
4. Paste the prepared text.

5. Click Generate.
6. Download the audio as an MP3 (a common audio file type).
Voiceover swaps: change a proven video's narration (its spoken words) into **another language**, while keeping the video itself.
Use a multilingual voice model (a voice that can speak many languages). **Check the supported languages** for any non-English video.
The voice should sound familiar to the target audience (the people you want to reach), such as a documentary-style voice.
Before producing audiobooks or other long audio for a store, **check how many characters** (letters, spaces and symbols the tool counts) or words the text-to-speech plan includes.

Choose the subscription tier (price level of a plan) so the full text can be converted without running out of allowance.
The $5 plan is limited to **50,000 characters** per month.
Opening several accounts instead of buying a higher plan to stay within a character limit can break the tool's terms of service (the rules you agree to when using it).
**Check the rules** before doing this.
Script Source
p.s: Video, ad creative and content production tools

p.t: Google Docs holds the script.
The creator checks fluency (how smoothly it reads), simplifies the language for listening and keeps the approved final text.
**Google Docs is the single source** for the text used in voice generation.
CapCut also has **built-in text-to-speech**.
AI video, avatar and script tools
ChatGPT (an AI chat tool) writes the video script from a prompt (your instruction).
The prompt specifies length, target age group, style reference and tone (the mood of the words).
**Have a knowledgeable reviewer check the script** for accuracy before use.
Midjourney (an AI image maker), used through Discord (a chat app), generates portrait images (face or figure pictures) of the character. It offers variations (new versions) of a chosen image.
It is used to create the avatar (the digital character) that will later be animated.
AI tools are used to produce faceless UGC (videos without a visible face) and viral short content (short clips meant to spread fast). This content is for the store's ads and social posts.
D-ID (an AI tool that makes a picture talk) animates a single portrait image with an uploaded audio file.

It moves the lips, blinks and adds facial expressions **automatically**.
The portrait does not need teeth or manual animation setup.
D-ID setup:

1. Upload the portrait image and the MP3 audio file.
2. Generate the talking video.
3. The output carries a watermark (a faint logo over the video) in the bottom left corner.
**Cover it before publishing.**
Video Generators
p.s: Video, ad creative and content production tools

p.t: Visla (an AI video tool) creates videos from text scripts and can produce stock-style footage (ready-made clip style footage).
It struggles with colloquial language (casual everyday speech).

At the time of writing, it was not yet reliable enough for finished ads. **It can still produce usable stock footage.**
Visla asks setup questions **before it generates a video**:

Aspect ratio (the shape of the frame, such as 16:9, 9:16 or 1:1)
The platform the video will be published on
The tone

The type of video (for example entertainment)
The medium
**Answering these first gives a more targeted result.**
Runway is an AI video editing tool. It can be used to edit product and marketing videos.
Pre-built AI platforms (ready-made AI tools) such as Arcads, Higgs Field and Motion come with built-in instructions for specific tasks.
They can create ads from a brand website, analyse ads, or research ads in public ad libraries (public collections where anyone can see ads).
Some allow **limited customisation** (changes).
Pre-built platforms can replace whole traditional roles, such as a designer or manual static ad production (making still image ads by hand). They work **without custom instructions**.
Choosing which platform to use, or whether to use one, requires knowing which are best and how to prompt them (how to write the instructions you type in).
Pre-built platforms work fairly similarly. **Trying one for a month** is a reasonable test before committing (paying for a long plan).
Captions and on-Screen text
p.s: Video, ad creative and content production tools

p.t: Vide.io (a caption tool) generates subtitles (on-screen text of the spoken words) **automatically** from an uploaded video.

It lets you choose subtitle style, size and font.
Its output is only a first draft and needs correction.
Vide.io (also written "vid.io") adds captions to videos, including bold, social-style caption formats.
**Use it to make short ad videos easier to follow with the sound off.**
Auto captioning (text made automatically from speech) in CapCut and Premiere Pro generates captions from the spoken audio. It **saves time** on manual text entry.
**Style auto captions after generating them.** This is step 5 of the CapCut ad order.
Platform-native text tools in Instagram, TikTok and YouTube Shorts add overlay text **when you upload**.
Premiere Pro (a professional video editor) has a TikTok-style text overlay (text placed on the video in TikTok's look).

Canva (an easy design app) is used for:
The landscape image layout (a wide image layout)

The simple logo
The text space
The thumbnail (a small preview picture), using its thumbnail templates (ready-made designs)

It **serves all static graphics** (still images, not moving) in the video.
Canva can be used to produce promotion ad creatives (ad designs).
Fiverr (a site for hiring freelancers) or similar freelance marketplaces can be used to **outsource them** (hand them to someone else).
Google Sheets (a free online spreadsheet) works for the 12-month offer calendar and for storing survey responses.

Canva Pro costs **11.99 USD per month**. It includes a stock video library (a store of ready-made clips).
It is a cheaper option when budget is tight.
Re-download AI-generated ads before uploading to Meta (the company behind Facebook and Instagram):
**Upload AI-generated ads** from ChatGPT or Claude to Canva, and re-download them before uploading to Meta.
This removes the metadata (hidden data) that Meta reads to detect AI-generated content. This prevents potential CPM penalties (CPM is the cost per 1,000 ad views, so penalties raise it).
It takes **2 minutes** and has no downside.

Use Photoshop or Illustrator (professional design programs) with an Envato Elements library (a subscription library of ready-made design files). **Use this when you need graphics and effects beyond Canva.**

p.t:

Procedure:
1. Go to ezgif.com.
2. Click Upload Video.
3. Select start and end time (in seconds or milliseconds).

4. Click Convert to GIF.
5. If the file size is too large, click Optimize and reduce quality (for example from quality 100 to 120).

6. Check that quality is acceptable and not pixelated (blocky).
7. Click Save or Download to save the GIF file.
Typical file reduction: 3.49 MB reduced to **1.27 MB** by quality adjustment.
Clipchamp was suggested as a free or low-cost video compression tool (a tool that makes a file smaller).
Paying a freelancer around **5 USD** on Fiverr to compress videos is much cheaper than buying a professional editing tool that costs around 300 USD.
